_source:
A real 'Literature in English Form 2 Scheme of Work' (a real Zambian secondary school's own department) was shared with this project via Drive, as three separate real documents -- one per term (Term 1, Term 2, Term 3), each carrying real calendar week-dates (e.g. 12/01/26 - 16/01/26). A teacher's name and two different department/organisation labels found in these documents' headers are not reproduced here per this app's standing sourcing policy. This is a genuine gap fill -- this app previously had no Literature in English Form 2 content at all (only Form 1 Terms 2-3). Cites the real official 'Literature Syllabus 2024 Form 1-4'.

A second, parallel real three-term document set (titled simply 'LITERATURE' rather than 'Literature in English', from the same real school and teacher but a differently-labelled department) was also found and read in full. It covers much of the same real ground (Topics 2.1 Zambian Literature and 2.2 Genres of Literature, the same real specific-competence numbering family) but is a rougher, less complete draft of the same underlying scheme -- e.g. its own Term 3 never reaches the Poetry genre at all (it stays entirely within Drama analysis and dramatisation before moving to revision), where the dated 'Literature in English' set used here does cover Poetry in full (types, elements, themes, verses, recitation, analysis, composition). Because it is superseded in coverage rather than independent, it was not used as an additional source and is not counted as a separate duplicate re-upload.

The source's own author list at 2.1.1.3 names real, published Zambian writers and their real published works (e.g. Kenneth Kaunda's 'Zambia Shall Be Free', Dominic Mulaisho's 'The Tongue of the Dumb') as literary-syllabus content -- these are public literary figures being taught as curriculum content, not personal/private information, so they are retained in the competency content itself (not in this _source field).

A genuine numbering irregularity in the source is preserved rather than silently fixed: the code '2.2.1.2' is used twice for two different things -- once as a stand-alone specific competence ('Draw Inferences from read texts') in Term 1 week 9, and again as the prefix for an entirely separate, deeper 'Elements of Prose' strand (2.2.1.2.1 through 2.2.1.2.8) spanning the rest of Term 1 and into Term 2. Both are kept here under their own sub-topic entries rather than merged or renumbered. Topic 2.2 (Genres of Literature) itself spans all three terms in the real source, moving from Prose (Term 1-2) through Drama (Term 2) to Poetry (Term 2-3); it is placed under whichever term the source actually teaches each strand in.

The back half of Term 3 (real scheme weeks 5-13) is a genuine, honestly-documented gap rather than fabricated content: after poetry composition, the source's own remaining weeks are comprehensive revision blocks (Zambian Literature, Prose, Drama, Poetry, cross-genre comparison, examination techniques, and a final review), each carrying no new specific-competence code of its own in the source -- consistent with the exclusion approach used elsewhere in this app for pure revision blocks. No separate Term 3 topic is invented here to fill that real gap.

Its own Content/Concept, Learning Activities, Strategies/Methods and Materials/Resources columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for every other bundled subject in this app.

subject.name: Literature in English
subject.description: Literature in English syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre, 2024).

grade.name: Form 2
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 2" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1.1 Development of Zambian Literature and Oral Traditions
sub_topics.description: The development of Zambian Literature (pre-independence and post-independence contexts) and Zambian oral traditions (folktales, myths, proverbs, songs) across ethnic groups (e.g. Bemba, Tonga, Lozi, Nyanja) and their role in preserving culture.

competencies.description: Explore the development of Zambian Literature, comparing pre-independence and post-independence works
Show understanding of different Zambian oral traditions and discuss their role in preserving culture
Analyse a Zambian oral tradition (folktale or proverb) critically for message, values and significance

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1.2 Themes in Zambian Literature
sub_topics.description: Themes of social issues (poverty, HIV/AIDS), identity and culture, colonialism and independence, and corruption, related to contemporary Zambian society.

competencies.description: Apply themes from Zambian Literature to real-life situations

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1.3 Zambian Authors, Playwrights and Poets
sub_topics.description: Prominent Zambian authors and their major works, and reading short excerpts from them.

competencies.description: Explore prominent Zambian authors, playwrights and poets and their contributions

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1.1 Fiction and Non-Fiction
sub_topics.description: Defining fiction (imaginary) and non-fiction (real events, people, setting) and distinguishing between them with examples.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of fiction and non-fiction

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1.2 Draw Inferences from Prose
sub_topics.description: Drawing inferences (moral lessons, values, attitudes) from read stories and applying them to real-life situations (e.g. honesty, perseverance).

competencies.description: Draw inferences from read stories accordingly

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1.3 Compose Fiction and Non-Fiction Stories
sub_topics.description: Composing a short story or personal narrative on cross-cutting themes (environmental health, entrepreneurship, corruption), with peer editing.

competencies.description: Compose fiction and non-fiction stories correctly

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1.2 Elements of Prose
sub_topics.description: Elements of prose (setting, plot, character, theme, point of view); creating own settings and composing own plots; demonstrating understanding of character types (protagonist, antagonist, major, minor, flat, round, dynamic, static, hero, villain). The source scheme reuses the code '2.2.1.2' both for the stand-alone 'Draw Inferences' competency above and as a prefix for this separate, deeper Elements-of-Prose strand (2.2.1.2.1-2.2.1.2.4 here); this real numbering collision is preserved rather than silently renumbered.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of the elements of prose
Create own settings for a story
Compose own plots for a story
Demonstrate understanding of character in prose

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1.2 Elements of Prose (continued)
sub_topics.description: Interpreting themes from different prose texts, analysing point of view, intensive analysis of a full prose passage, and composing a complete prose story incorporating all elements.

competencies.description: Interpret themes from different texts
Analyse text for point of view
Analyse prose intensively
Compose prose stories creatively

sub_topics.name: 2.2.2.1 Types of Drama
sub_topics.description: Tragedy (hero fails/dies), comedy (happy ending), tragicomedy (mix), with examples from known plays or films.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of different types of drama

sub_topics.name: 2.2.2.2 Elements of Drama
sub_topics.description: Plot, character, theme, dialogue, setting, act, and staging; plot structure (exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution); character types; theme and characteristics of effective dialogue.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of the elements of drama
Analyse plot in drama
Demonstrate understanding of character in drama and analyse characters
Analyse theme in drama and demonstrate understanding of dialogue

sub_topics.name: 2.2.2.3 Analysis and Dramatisation of Drama
sub_topics.description: Analysing a one-act play for plot, characters, theme, dialogue and setting (cross-cutting themes: climate change, corruption); rehearsing and performing it.

competencies.description: Analyse drama and dramatise plays skilfully

sub_topics.name: 2.2.3.1 Types of Poetry
sub_topics.description: Lyric (personal feelings), narrative (tells a story), ode (praise), elegy (mourning), ballad (song-like), sonnet (14 lines).

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of different types of poetry

sub_topics.name: 2.2.3.2 Elements of Poetry
sub_topics.description: Stanza, verse, rhyme, rhythm, imagery, and figurative language (simile, metaphor, personification), introduced here and continued into Term 3.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of the elements of poetry

sub_topics.name: 2.2.3.2 Poetry: Themes, Verses and Recitation
sub_topics.description: Interpreting themes conveyed through imagery and figurative language, writing own stanzas, writing own verses, and reciting poems (praise, ode, lyric, elegy).

competencies.description: Interpret themes in poetry and write own stanzas
Write own verses and recite poems skilfully

sub_topics.name: 2.2.3.2 Analysis and Composition of Poetry
sub_topics.description: Analysing poems for sound devices (alliteration, assonance, onomatopoeia), imagery, figures of speech and structure; composing poems (praise, ode, lyric, elegy) on cross-cutting themes (climate change, financial education, corruption, HIV/AIDS, drug abuse) and exhibiting them.

competencies.description: Analyse poems accordingly
Compose poems accordingly
